football_evidence.question: Can Coastal Carolina’s pass rush get to Malachi Singleton?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Coastal Carolina, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.7 of the 3.5 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When App State has the ball (big plays on the ground): App State’s offense turns 1.8% of its runs into explosive gains, and Coastal Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Coastal Carolina has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Coastal Carolina’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 12.9% of its runs, and App State’s defense stops 19.8% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When App State has the ball (third down): App State’s offense converts 28.5% of its third downs, and Coastal Carolina’s defense allows opponents to convert 44.9% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).
In his last two games (NC State and Old Dominion), Singleton averaged 6.3 yards per attempt, against 9.6 in his three games before that.
contradicting: When Coastal Carolina has the ball (big plays on the ground): Coastal Carolina’s offense turns 7.4% of its runs into explosive gains, and App State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 3.8% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Coastal Carolina has the ball (big plays through the air): Coastal Carolina’s offense turns 11.1% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and App State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).

When App State has the ball (the red zone): App State’s offense succeeds on 62.2% of its red-zone plays, and Coastal Carolina’s defense allows success on 42.7% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.8%).

When App State has the ball (big plays through the air): App State’s offense turns 11.9% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Coastal Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 13.2% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).
quarterbacks: Deuce Bailey has completed 93 of 174 passes (53.4%) for 1,352 yards, 7.8 yards per attempt, 13 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for Coastal Carolina, and has been sacked on 18 of 192 dropbacks.

Malachi Singleton has completed 101 of 155 passes (65.2%) for 1,278 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 1 interception in five games for App State, and has been sacked on 5 of 160 dropbacks.
